items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: They got whites who would ignore Bix in preference of Lurie or Henry Bussey or Tony, Lurie Pinnico, you dig, B.A. Rolf.

ctx.x: Seeing as how Armstrong, can you hold it over here soon? Did I just want to give it a hand? Seeing as how, you know, Armstrong went up to Chicago and made a big name for himself, in a way, he sort of put himself above that, all that competitiveness and savage competition when he became famous. And I'm just wondering if, do you think he ever took his fame for granted or was he always trying to expand it?

No, he was a happy man. He, he was so acclaimed by everybody. Every trumpet player, everybody who, who, who played a horn, paid him homage somewhere or other, or they stayed a distance from him. Whole lot of great white trumpet players, legitimate trumpet players, never went near Louis. You dig, they may have looked, but they dismissed him as, not exactly black, but that kind of style, that ain't, well, that's something to do with it too, but you always, you don't always put it on being black. He could have been…
Was Johnny Dunn from New Orleans?
